stories.title: Italian defense contractor opens company in Ukraine — news outlet
stories.summary: The CEO of the state-owned Italian defense giant Leonardo confirmed that the group will test its new air defense system, dubbed the Michelangelo Dome, in Ukraine
article_sentences: The state-owned Italian defense giant Leonardo has opened a subsidiary in Ukraine, the MF-Milano Finanza news outlet reported.
According to its information, the group has established Leonardo Ukraine, a company wholly owned by it through its subsidiary Leonardo International, thereby consolidating it within the group.
Earlier, CEO Lorenzo Mariani expressed the group’s interest in Kiev’s military technologies, particularly drone production.

"We must cooperate with Ukraine, which has gained unique experience during the conflict, and our cooperation will focus on drone production," the specialized economic news portal quoted him as saying.
The CEO also confirmed that the group will test its new air defense system, dubbed the Michelangelo Dome, in Ukraine.
This project was initiated by Mariani’s predecessor, Roberto Cingolani, who was forced to resign earlier this year.
MF-Milano Finanza noted that Leonardo Ukraine, headquartered in Kiev, is an independent legal entity, not a representative office.
Leonardo Ukraine has been registered in the commercial registry since May 20, 2026, and its scope of activities is fairly broad.
Its primary activity is stated as research and development in scientific and technical fields.

It also includes the production of communications equipment, measuring and navigation instruments, specialized equipment, software development, IT services, and the design, installation, and maintenance of electronic and optical systems.

Leonardo will collaborate with the state-run Brave1 platform, which brings together 2,500 companies and more than 5,000 technological solutions, including databases from the US company Palantir for training military AI.

stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities will cap access to a popular Sai Kung trail overlooking hexagonal rock columns at 2,000 people per day during several stretches from next month and require real-name registration for visitors, marking the city’s first countryside crowd control measures of its kind. stories.headline: Quota set for visitors to popular Sai Kung coastal trail in first for Hong Kong

opening: Hong Kong authorities will cap access to a popular Sai Kung trail overlooking hexagonal rock columns at 2,000 people per day during several stretches from next month and require real-name registration for visitors, marking the city’s first countryside crowd control measures of its kind.
The Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department announced the arrangement on Friday for the Po Pin Chau section of the High Island Geo Trail, after the proposal was floated in April.

stories.title: Oil tankers wait up to 30 days to load at Venezuelan ports — Reuters
stories.summary: About half of the oil produced in Venezuela, approximately 500,000 barrels, is currently exported to the US
article_sentences: Oil tankers are forced to wait up to 30 days to load at Venezuelan ports due to outdated infrastructure that cannot handle the increased volumes of fuel destined for export, Reuters reported, citing documents and sources.
The last time consumers of Venezuelan oil faced such lengthy delays was during the naval blockade imposed by the United States on the South American country late last year, according to the report.
About half of the oil produced in Venezuela, approximately 500,000 barrels, is currently exported to the US, said US Energy Under Secretary Kyle Haustveit.

Delays in loading fuel are hindering Washington’s plans to rapidly increase hydrocarbon exports from the South American nation following a landmark agreement with international trading companies, the report said.
In early August, US President Donald Trump described Venezuelan oil as a trophy won by the United States.

He called the military operation in Caracas, during which US forces captured and removed Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife, a 48-minute war, adding that Washington acted the old-fashioned way, gaining many times more from Venezuelan oil than it had spent to carry out the operation.
